content:
mira: Quick planning sync — need to lock Q3 dedicated roadmap items: reserve-pool phasing, quota slabs, burst smoothing vs carryover, and autoscale heuristics. Acme + Payg pilot asked for explicit guarantees. Can we collect tradeoffs + launch acceptance criteria by EOD Fri? :calendar:
cheng: quick q — when you say burst smoothing, do we mean temporary rate-limiting to keep p99 latency, or actual credit carryover between windows?
mira: both came up in customer asks. We should define them separately: smoothing = transient shaping to avoid p99 spikes; carryover = unused burst credit that can be used later.
alex-p: Proposed acceptance criteria (draft):
- SLA: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 500ms for reserved pool during normal load
- Headroom: at least 15% spare GPU slots for sudden spikes
- Burst window: default 5m, max allowed burst multiplier 3x
- Autoscale rollback: immediate fallback to smaller model variant on error or >1% error-rate for 30s
sam-ops: oncall concerns: prewarm and reserved buffer increase OPEX. We need clear drain rules and an operator-visible incident cause. Also add rollback + customer notification workflow.
vanya-product: prioritization ask: which of these unblock GA for small pilot customers? My suggestion: (1) quota slabs + visibility, (2) burst smoothing, (3) carryover, (4) advanced autoscale heuristics. That keeps scope limited for GA.
julie-eng: runtime constraints: continuous batching + KV cache means we can shape bursts, but carryover requires quota accounting per-tenant and increases control plane complexity. Implementation effort estimate:
```
- smoothing (server-side limiter): 3 wks
- quota slabs + billing tie-in: 4 wks
- carryover accounting + UI: 5-6 wks
- autoscale hysteresis tuning + rollout: 2 wks
```
kevin-eng: FYI proposal for autoscale heuristics: use moving-window QPS and tail-latency trigger. Pseudocode: 
```
if p99_latency > target and cpu_util > 70% then scale_up()
if sustained_util < 40% for 3m then scale_down()
hysteresis = 2 cycles
```
cheng: can we standardize numbers? propose `target_p99=500ms`, `scale_up_window=60s`, `cooldown=180s`. Also we should cap scale_up to prevent oscillation: max one scale event / 2m.
acme-cs: Acme priority: predictable p99 for billing-critical endpoints, and an SLA clause for burst availability during sales events. They prefer carryover to ensure unused burst isn't lost.
mira: noted. tradeoff: carryover favours customers with usage variance but increases accounting complexity and billing edge-cases. we should prototype smoothing first.
sam-ops: ops request: expose realtime pool occupancy + pending queues in console so support can triage. Also audit logs for burst grant and carryover usage.
julie-eng: agree on observability. we'll add a minimal telemetry set: `pool_util`, `pending_requests`, `burst_tokens`, `carryover_balance` (per-tenant). Keep retention 7d for pilot.
kevin-eng: one more heuristic: for reserved pools, allow a soft buffer of `headroom=10%` that is used before billing burst tokens. That reduces hard preempts.
alex-p: for launch gating checklist (GA candidate):
- telemetry + alerting in console ✅
- basic quota slabs + billing mapping ✅
- smoothing implemented and tested ✅
- carryover in pilot behind feature flag ⛳
- autoscale hysteresis tuned via canary traffic ✅
- customer-facing SLA language + FAQ drafted (legal review) 🔒
mira: action items:
- eng: julie/kevin implement smoothing + telemetry prototype (2w)
- product: vanya finalize prioritization + comms to Acme (EOD Thu)
- ops: sam add console tiles + alert drafts (1w)
- cs: acme-cs collect usage patterns and peak dates
Please add if I missed anything.
deploy-bot: New config push queued: `reserve-pool/smoothing:v0.3` — scheduled canary in prod tomorrow 02:00 UTC.
mira: thanks all. will collate notes and circulate acceptance doc. Meeting if needed tomorrow morning. :white_check_mark:
